title.narrative: Inclusive Growth in Mozambique Phase III (2025-2028)
Inkluderande tillväxt i Mocambique Fas III (2025-2028)

description.narrative: IGM is a research and capacity development programme implemented by the National Directorate of Economic and Development Policies (DNPED) of the Ministry of Planning and Development of Mozambique (MPD) and the Centre for Economic and Management Studies (CEEG) of the Faculty of Economics of the Eduardo Mondlane University (UEM), in partnership with the United Nations University World Institute for Development Economics Research (UNU-WIDER). The overarching aim of the programme is to enhance the Mozambican government’s capabilities and policy processes to address economic policy challenges over the short-, medium- and long-term. This phase III will focus on developing local capacity and producing evidence to support improved macroeconomic management, pro-poor public revenue and spending, and development of concrete policy options to raise the wellbeing of the poorest through sustained and inclusive economic growth.

IGM är ett forsknings- och kapacitetsutvecklingsprogram som genomförs av det nationella direktoratet för ekonomisk och utvecklingspolitik (DNPED) vid Moçambiques ministerium för planering och utveckling (MPD) och Centre for Economic and Management Studies (CEEG) vid Eduardo Mondlane University (UEM), i samarbete med United Nations University World Institute for Development Economics Research (UNU-WIDER). Det övergripande syftet med programmet är att förbättra den moçambikiska regeringens kapacitet och politiska processer för att hantera ekonomiska politiska utmaningar på kort, medellång och lång sikt. Denna fas III kommer att fokusera på att utveckla lokal kapacitet och ta fram bevis för att stödja förbättrad makroekonomisk förvaltning, offentliga inkomster och utgifter för de fattiga, och utveckling av konkreta politiska alternativ för att öka välbefinnandet för de fattigaste genom hållbar och inkluderande ekonomisk tillväxt.

The overarching aim of Phase III of the IGM programme (2025-2028) is to enhance the Mozambican governments capabilities and policy processes to address the economic policy challenges over the short, medium and long-term. Phase III will focus on developing local capacity and producing evidence to support improved macroeconomic management, pro-poor public revenue and spending, and development of concrete policy options to raise the well being of the poorest through sustained and inclusive economic growth. IGM will maintain its critical support to the Government of Mozambique to adopt stronger evidence-based economic policies, but also with emphasis on medium- and long-term strategic thinking and planning, which will contribute to broader-based sustainable development.
The specific objectives of IGM Phase III are to:
1) Produce rigorous evidence to address key policy challenges and inform Mozambiques development strategy over the next decades (evidence generation).
2) Develop research and analytical capabilities at MPD, as well as in local academia, to support stronger evidence-based policy (capacity development).
3) Stimulate policy uptake, engaging key policymakers across multiple fora to drive policy debate and evidence-informed decision-making (policy engagement & communication).
These objectives will be reached by focusing on three thematic areas; Poverty Inequality and social protection; Macroeconomics; and Public Finance. The two cross-cutting themes concerning economic policy challenges of preparing for and adapting to Climate Change, and considerations about Gender Inclusiveness in economic policy will be explicitly addressed in all areas of work.
